terms.definition: The green organelle inside plant cells that captures sunlight to make food.
terms.function: Carries out photosynthesis to make sugar for the plant.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the green cells of leaves and other plant parts.
terms.whyItMatters: It turns sunlight into the food that feeds the plant and nearly all life.

terms.definition: The green pigment in the chloroplast that captures energy from sunlight.
terms.whereItIs: Coating the thylakoid discs of the chloroplast.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what makes plants green and lets them capture the light they need.

terms.definition: The flat, green discs inside a chloroplast, stacked into groups called grana.
terms.function: Catch the sunlight and begin making the food.
terms.whereItIs: Stacked inside the chloroplast's stroma fluid.
terms.whyItMatters: They are where the light part of photosynthesis happens.

terms.definition: The fluid space inside a chloroplast around the stacks of discs.
terms.function: Holds the grana and helps build the food.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the chloroplast, filling around the grana.
terms.whyItMatters: The stroma is where the sugar-making steps are completed.

terms.definition: The process in chloroplasts that uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and oxygen.
terms.function: Makes food for the plant and releases oxygen.
terms.whereItIs: In the chloroplasts of plant cells.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the source of food and oxygen for most life on Earth.
